description:
We are a technology-driven team participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, working on Planet X and SPHEREx. Our goal is to build an interactive web platform that visualizes SPHEREx observations over time and helps explore potential moving celestial objects using image analysis and AI-assisted techniques.

We welcome members interested in astrophysics, Python, AI/ML, web development, data analysis, visualization, and UI/UX. Let's explore the universe through data and innovation!
summary:
COSMIC PULSE is designed to help people interact with real SPHEREx data. This shows you how scientific evidence is analysed. COSMIC PULSE was made for the NASA Space Apps Challenge for the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge. It links space observations to methods allowing users to view images, look at coordinates, find sources and compare observations.

You can view real SPHEREx FITS images and see the actual data. You can see how bright different areas of the image are. It will run a source detection algorithm to highlight potential sources to investigate. However, it will also show you what it cannot do, for example there is no comparison time, uncertainty and it just detects sources.

We aim to make astronomical data more accessible, understandable and reproducible. Whilst we cannot find or confirm Planet X, it provides a transparent starting point to begin looking into the observations and learning how astronomers analyse evidence.
details:
# COSMIC PULSE

## What was created?

A public facing astronomy investigation tool using NASA's SPHEREx data.

This application allows users to search for observations, view scientific images, detect sources within and investigate evidence.

The workflow includes:

1. Search

2. View

3. Time Travel

4. Investigate

5. Interpret

Within the application there are a few key components:

1. Cosmic Explorer

Allows users to search for information about astronomical observations, right ascension and declination and the products available.

2. Cosmic Time Machine

Allows users to view what epochs were taken during the observation. It currently identifies if there is only one usable epoch and does not allow multiple epochs to be compared.

3. Discovery Lab

This will process a real FITS image taken from SPHEREx to estimate the background, detect possible sources, identify the positions of these sources and measure their apertures. This observation contains 4364 detections that meet the criteria and only the top 200 are returned to the user. This is shown on the interface.

4. Scientific FITS Image Viewer

This will show a preview of the image. Users can adjust the stretch of the image, view the image and see the scientific information.

5. Evidence Capsules

A section that can be used in the future to create shareable, repeatable investigations.

## How it works

The application pulls information from SPHEREx observations using the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA). This allows access to a real multi-extension FITS file. Users can view the image, variance, flags and any other extensions that are available.

The backend will then process the scientific image. This will include background estimation, finding objects that are above the detectable threshold and grouping these together. This will then identify the centres of the sources and measure their apertures and return this to be viewed in the Discovery Lab.

This application will not automatically classify detected sources as new planets, transients or discoveries. It differentiates between sources found by the algorithm and actual astronomical objects.

## Why it's useful

Large astronomical surveys can have lots of observations. By making these observations more understandable and easier to view, it can help students, teachers and members of the public get involved with real astronomical data.

This application aims to make the data from the mission easier to understand and investigate. It will highlight what information is available for the observations, what units are being used, how it has been processed and what limitations are known.

## Technologies used

Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS

Backend: Python, FastAPI

Scientific Processing: NumPy, SciPy, Pillow, FITS/WCS processing.

Data: NASA SPHEREx Observations (IRSA)

Format: FITS (Flexible Image Transport System)

Hosting: Vercel, Render

Version Control: Git, GitHub

## What makes it creative?

Rather than having images of observations, this application will present the observations in an investigation format. It will give users the ability to view scientific images, see information about the observations, investigate with right ascension and declination, detect sources and identify limitations in the data quality.

This project has focused on scientific integrity. It will tell users when there isn't any comparison data available, identify that there are limited sources found and will not automatically class sources found by the algorithm as discoveries.

## Current capabilities and future impact

This deployed prototype will show how a real SPHEREx observation can be processed and viewed. The Time Machine currently doesn't have more than one confirmed usable epoch so it cannot show real changes across multiple epochs. There is also more work to be done on validating the sources using astrometry and estimating uncertainty in the detected sources.

This application can be developed further to include more observations, multiple epochs, more uncertainty handling and repeatable evidence. This means it could be a useful tool for education and investigation of large scale astronomical data.
